answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller, including plume, ember, and willow, to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Creating another identity requires another bond, and closing an account does not release funds early. An attacker operating 1,000 fake sellers must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, paying financing costs even if none wins work. This makes mass identity creation costly without claiming to eliminate it.
